$doc: Gate 4g — ADVISORY anchor audit. This gate never fails a build. It reports;
it does not decide. B4 measured 597 correct English anchors against 55 genuine
corrections in `ja` alone, so anchor correctness is not enumerable and a blocking
anchor check would fail on proper nouns indefinitely (NATIVE_REVIEW methodology,
closing paragraph). Everything below is data; the gate contains no string tests.
identities: repository-approved English text that may legitimately appear as anchor
text. The gate ALSO reads i18n-gates/4f-headings.json `licensed.global` and unions
it in, so the repository keeps ONE frozen proper-noun registry rather than two that
can drift apart. Only anchor-surface identities that 4f has no reason to carry are
listed here. `global` applies to every locale; a per-locale list applies to that
locale alone — which is how the `ja` place-name policy (B3: only Vernal and state
names are transliterated, every other city stays Latin) is encoded without
flattening it. `Vernal` and `Utah` are therefore identities in six locales and
deliberately NOT in `ja`, where a bare Latin `Vernal` anchor would be drift.
markers[locale]: English anchor tokens occurring >=3x in the EN rendered anchor
corpus AND in ZERO anchors of that locale, derived at P38 from the 6,100-anchor
per-locale rendered corpus and then FROZEN — the same derivation, and the same
freezing rationale, as gate 4f. Re-derived at run time, an introduced English
anchor would add its own tokens to the locale vocabulary and delete the markers
that should have caught it. This is a REGRESSION signal and reports zero on the
corpus it was derived from, by construction.
nativeMarkers[locale]: the mirror image — tokens occurring >=3x in that locale’s
anchors and in ZERO English anchors. Latin-script locales only: they are what lets
the gate see target-language content in an anchor that has no script signal. For
`ja`/`zh` the script test governs instead, so no list is carried.
repeatThreshold: distinct pages above which an English-identical anchor is treated as
systemic (template, chrome, or a house loanword) rather than one-off drift. Set to 5
from the measured corpus: no B4-class content drift exceeded 3 pages per distinct
string, while structural surfaces (breadcrumb, nav, related-content runs) span 60-77.
A locale registered in i18n.ts with no entry here is a hard exit 2 — never a silent
pass (the `ja` UI-chrome fail-open lesson, handoff §7 Gate 4a). Exit 2 is the only
non-zero exit this gate can produce, and it means the gate could not run, never that
the corpus is wrong.
Attested in the rendered anchor corpus and in the decisions that produced it —
B3 (ja place names), B4 (the 597 retained proper-noun anchors), P11.1 (the
author-bio exception) and the language switcher, whose endonyms are untranslated
by definition. Nothing here is an invented rule: each entry is text the repository
already ships as an anchor and has already decided to keep.
Censused at P38 and deliberately NOT registered, so a later phase does not re-propose
them. Each is English anchor text a reviewer should keep seeing.
`Home` — 142 anchors on 77 `it` pages is the shipped value of the `it` `nav.home`
dictionary key, but 2 anchors on 2 `zh` pages are hardcoded against `zh` `nav.home`
= 首页. Registering `Home` would mask the second while excusing the first.
`Guides` — 142 anchors on 77 `fr` pages; French and English spell it identically, so
registering it would license the same string in the five locales where it is drift.
`Dinosaur Country` — a 4i lock in `ja` (first-use gloss) and a live `de` defect (A10).
Registering it globally would mask the class A10 belongs to.
`State Park`, `Reservoir`, `Byway` as bare heads — always seen inside a registered
full name; registering the head alone would license it everywhere.
